claims.text: Atomic layer deposition can produce atomically dispersed platinum on a ceria-zirconia support.
Atomically dispersed platinum on ceria-zirconia will enhance catalytic activity under automotive exhaust conditions.
Atomically dispersed platinum on ceria-zirconia will improve catalyst durability under automotive exhaust conditions.
The intervention will reduce the platinum loading required.
Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use platinum nanoparticles dispersed on alumina supports.
Ceria-zirconia provides stronger metal-support interactions than the baseline support.
Ceria-zirconia has oxygen-storage capacity that helps maintain platinum dispersion.
The support-mediated interactions inhibit platinum sintering during thermal cycling.
Atomically dispersed platinum maximizes effective catalytic surface area per platinum atom.
Strong platinum-ceria-zirconia interactions stabilize platinum sites against agglomeration and sintering during thermal and redox cycling.
Suppression of agglomeration and sintering sustains catalytic performance while permitting lower platinum content.
The modified catalyst will achieve catalytic conversion rates similar to or better than those of conventional platinum-on-alumina.
The modified catalyst will have durability similar to or better than that of conventional platinum-on-alumina.
The modified catalyst can provide the predicted performance while using approximately 30–50% less platinum.
The predicted benefit should hold at approximately 600–800 °C during redox cycling in the presence of NOx, CO, and hydrocarbons.
Atypically aggressive aging or loss of ceria-zirconia structural integrity may diminish the performance benefit.
Failure to attain equivalent conversion and durability with at least 30% less platinum would falsify the hypothesis.
